fixes.explanation: You got it, baker. She opens that basket, sees a crying little boy, and says, “This is one of the Hebrew children.” (Exodus 2:6) She knew exactly who he was. And the verse says she had compassion on him. Her father's whole palace is running on one rule, and she's standing there holding a baby.

Egyptian is a fair guess, friend. She's Pharaoh's daughter, standing on the Nile, so you'd expect that word. But she opens the basket and says, “This is one of the Hebrew children.” (Exodus 2:6) She could tell right away he wasn't one of hers. And the verse says she had compassion on him anyway.

Midianite, baker? That one's coming out of left field. I love the confidence, though. In this scene she opens the basket and says, “This is one of the Hebrew children.” (Exodus 2:6) That's the word she used. Midianites don't show up until later in the story, and I'm not telling you how. The story isn't over.

Desert, baker? I get it, a lot of Moses's story happens out in dry country. But not here. She names him Moses and explains, “I drew him out of the water.” (Exodus 2:10) This baby came out of the Nile, and not one grain of sand in this scene. The story isn't over, though.

Mountains, friend? You're aiming way too high. This boy was pulled out of a river, not off a peak. She named him Moses and explained, “I drew him out of the water.” (Exodus 2:10) A basket in the reeds, a splash and a name. I've been stuck in a drawer, and even I know water when I see it.
